subject: Training usage & data retention Qs — FintechCo
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@fintechco.com>

Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 14:12:03 -0500
Subject: Training usage and data retention — quick Qs

Hi Aditya,

We’re moving through a security review and I have a few clarifying questions about Redwood’s policies before legal signs off: 

1) Do you ever use customer-provided inputs (requests, uploads, files) to train or fine-tune any Redwood models or to improve model weights?
2) What is the default retention window for request payloads, logs, and generated outputs? Is that configurable per-account?
3) If we request deletion, what is the SLA for removing all customer content from live systems, backups, and logs? Do you provide an audit record/proof?
4) For hosted deployments, what residency guarantees exist (region of storage and processing)? Are snapshots/backups ever replicated outside the chosen region?

We prefer clear contractual language around training usage and deletion guarantees. Appreciate a concise response — if easier, happy to schedule a short call.

Regards,
Alice Monroe
Head of Security, FintechCo
alice.monroe@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@fintechco.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Training usage and data retention — quick Qs

Hi Alice — thanks for the questions. Below are the precise, operational responses you can include in your review; I’ll also summarize suggested contract language at the bottom.

1) Training usage: Redwood does NOT use Customer Data (defined as any text, file, or content submitted by the Customer via our API or UI) to train, fine-tune, or update the weights of any models used in the Redwood hosted service. This applies to both prompt inputs and model outputs. We separate telemetry used for service health (error rates, latency percentiles) and aggregated anonymized metrics from Customer Data. Any telemetry that could contain user content is treated as Customer Data and handled per retention rules below.

2) Default retention windows and configurability:
  - Request payloads & full response bodies: default retention is 30 days for hosted customers.
  - Structured logs (latency, token counts, error codes): retained 365 days by default for billing and SLO analysis.
  - Embeddings/derived artifacts: treated as Customer Data and retained per the same window as payloads unless otherwise agreed.
  - These defaults are configurable at account level for hosted customers (can be reduced to 0 days / no retention for request bodies; structured logs retention can be reduced with contract addendum). Dedicated and Private deployments are configurable by the customer — in Private, retention is controlled by customer config and local policies.

3) Deletion SLA and proof:
  - Deletion API: Customers can call the Redwoods Delete endpoint to remove stored request/response content.
  - SLA: For hosted accounts, we will purge data from active serving and indexing within 72 hours of a verified deletion request.
  - Backups & snapshots: backups are rotated; primary backup retention is up to 90 days by default for operational recovery. Upon a deletion request we mark records for purge and scrub eligible records from backups according to the following workflow: we remove the data from active stores within 72 hours and schedule targeted removal from backups; final sanitization of older backups may take up to 30 days depending on the backup rotation cycle.
  - Audit evidence: We provide a deletion confirmation package (time-stamped audit log entries, storage keys/IDs removed, and the API request that triggered the action). If you need a signed attestation or a custom deletion SLA, we can add that to the contract.

4) Data residency and snapshot replication:
  - Hosted: customers choose region(s) where requests are processed and stored. We do not replicate customer content across regions unless explicitly enabled for DR.
  - Backups: by default backups are stored in the same region; cross-region replication is only enabled with customer consent or for specific enterprise DR settings in the Dedicated product.
  - Private/Dedicated: data residency is fully under customer control (VPC/on-prem).

Additional notes:
  - Subprocessors: We maintain a subprocessors list and will provide it via the standard SSO portal. Any critical subprocessors (cloud provider storage, KMS) are listed in the SOC2 package.
  - KMS & encryption: Customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS; we also support Bring-Your-Own-Key for enterprise contracts.

Suggested contract language (short):
  - "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train or improve any models or model weights without Customer's prior written consent."
  - "Customer Data will be deleted from active systems within seventy-two (72) hours of a verified deletion request; Redwood will provide deletion confirmation and associated audit artifacts."

I’ve attached the one-pager and SOC2 report already shared by Aditya and included links to the retention documentation. Happy to join the call on 11/7.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Training usage and data retention — quick Qs

Thanks Marissa — that helps. A couple follow-ups before we loop legal:

• Can you confirm the backup purge timeline is part of the deletion promise (we need to present an end-to-end worst-case timeline to our risk committee)?
• If we require a 30-day max backup retention, can you accommodate that for hosted?
• We’ll also need a process for providing proof-of-deletion for an individual user record (not just bulk deletes). Does the audit package include object IDs and timestamps that we can map back to our internal IDs?

If you can confirm those items in writing I’ll forward to Legal for contract clauses. Also please include the subprocessors list for Hosted.

Best,
Alice

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Training usage and data retention — quick Qs

Hi Alice — follow-up and next steps:

1) Backup purge timeline: confirmed as part of the deletion promise. Operationally: active removal within 72 hours; targeted backup sanitization completed within 30 days worst-case; we will provide the worst-case timeline in the deletion confirmation artifact.

2) 30-day max backup retention for Hosted: yes — we can commit to a 30-day max backup retention for your account as part of the enterprise configuration. We will add this to the SOW/Appendix.

3) Proof-of-deletion for individual records: the deletion confirmation package contains the object/storage IDs, timestamps, and request-id fields that map to the API call; we can add a step to include your internal ID mapping if you provide the mapping keys.

4) Subprocessors: attaching the subprocessors list and a DSAR/deletion request template that legal teams typically use.

Next steps: I’ll share a redlined clause for the MSA and an SOW appendix that sets retention/backups; propose we lock these items in this week so procurement can route.

Attachments: dsar_deletion_template.docx, soc2_report_redwood_2025.pdf

Talk soon —
Aditya
